title: Vision notes
description: The output of deck-builder's vision pass — what turns a PDF page or image from something Claude merely READ in conversation (uncitable) into evidence retrieval can shortlist and a slide can cite. Before this file exists, ingest_sources.py-style flows flag a PDF/image `read_natively` and the knowledge stays in the transcript, with no chunk_id for QA to check. Each entry here is a citable unit: a slide block's `sources[]` can name a note_id exactly as it names a text chunk_id, and deck_index.py's `vision_note_to_chunk()` makes every note retrievable.

note_id.description: Stable id, e.g. 'v1', 'v2' — what a slide block's sources[] cites.

source_ref.description: The source document this page/image came from.

page.description: 1-indexed page number, or 1 for a standalone image.

region.description: Optional — a sub-region of the page the note is about, as 0-1 fractions, same convention as training-material-generator's annotation bboxes.

transcription.description: What the model actually read off the page, in prose — the citable claim. Never left empty; a page with nothing worth transcribing gets no note.

structured.description: Optional structured extraction — rows for a table, {nodes, edges} for a diagram/org-chart. Free-form; deck_index.py folds this into the chunk's text via JSON dump when present, so it's still searchable even before a caller writes a bespoke reader for it.

confidence.description: 'low' means the transcription is a best-effort read of something unclear (poor scan, ambiguous diagram) — plan_deck.py's provenance gate refuses to let a low-confidence note be the SOLE source for a non-gap claim (deck-builder test case #19); it must be paired with a supporting text source, or the claim marked gap.
